title: Liapoldus Core bootstrap core.yaml
description: Минимальная bootstrap-конфигурация Core. Plugin settings и fixed endpoints хранятся в SQLite; оператор вручную запускает Core и plugins. Core не управляет plugin processes или containers.

fileReference.description: External file reference; inline secret values are forbidden.

path.description: Local SQLite database file path; network filesystems are not supported.

clientCA.description: Required for web Controller non-loopback access; desktop uses restricted SSH forwarding to loopback.

tls.description: Management TLS identity is required for every bind. Web Controller traffic additionally uses client mTLS and Bearer service credential.

plugins.description: Operator-declared plugin instances and their replicas. This list is the only source of fixed replica endpoints and expected mTLS identities. It is static for the lifetime of the Core process: changing it requires editing core.yaml and restarting Core. Core has no plugin registration API and does not accept plugin self-registration.

replicaClientCRLs.description: Optional signed CRL files checked against replicaClientCA. If configured, unreadable, expired or invalid CRLs fail closed. Changes take effect after restarting Core.

replicaServerCRLs.description: Optional signed CRL files checked against replicaServerCA. If configured, unreadable, expired or invalid CRLs fail closed. Changes take effect after restarting Core.

pluginControl.description: Private Plugin SDK lifecycle/configuration REST listener. Its trust roots are independent from Management and plugin-to-plugin roots. certificate/key are Core's own identity, served on the pull listener and presented to replicas when Core dials them. replicaClientCA verifies replica client certificates on the pull listener; replicaServerCA verifies replica server certificates when Core dials a declared endpoint. Optional signed CRL sets are independently bound to each trust root and fail closed when configured. Credential, CA and CRL file changes require an orderly Core restart in v1.

pluginIdentifier.description: Stable operator-assigned identifier. Not a product, capability or provider name.

endpoint.description: Fixed origin Core dials for Plugin SDK control calls. Core never derives or discovers an endpoint.

peerIdentity.description: Expected mTLS identity of one replica. Core compares it exactly against the verified certificate, in both directions. An absent entry is never a wildcard.

x-liapoldus-invariants: Core is a single process and SQLite is the only durable source of desired plugin configuration.
Plugin processes and their binaries are operator-managed. Core only connects to fixed registered endpoints and has no process, binary-installation or container-provider management API.

The plugins list in core.yaml is the single normative source of plugin instance ids, replica ids, fixed endpoints and expected mTLS identities. Core has no plugin registration API, does not accept plugin self-registration, and treats the list as static for the process lifetime.

A replica identity document published by a plugin is conformance evidence only. It never registers a replica, never overrides a declared endpoint or expected identity, and never becomes desired state.
Plugin settings are not accepted in core.yaml, environment variables, argv, or plugin application-config files; plugins pull exact immutable versioned JSON from Core REST after Reload(generation).
Traffic listeners, sites, routes, and traffic-plugin runtime configuration are not part of core.yaml.
Traffic plugins own their runtime state on persistent local storage; Core remains implementation-agnostic.
Local process supervision, signed package installation, container providers and workload automation are deferred to v2.
Management TLS is always enabled. Management and plugin workload trust roots are separate.
Plugin control REST uses the pluginControl TLS files and does not reuse the Management client CA or plugin-to-plugin trust roots.
SQLite and plugin-owned runtime state use persistent local storage; Core has no plugin package cache.
Plaintext secret values are forbidden in core.yaml and plugin settings JSON; secrets are returned only by scoped Core REST grants.
